headline: High-risk workflow automation pair: n8n can execute commands and write files, creating dangerous default interaction and cascading-action risks with Airflow-driven outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has no browser or clipboard bridge and no documented direct ingestion of n8n outputs, so a prompt-injection path is not default. However, n8n can write files and call APIs, so if operators manually pass Airflow-generated content into n8n workflows, malicious content could be reinterpreted. The pathway is interaction-dependent and small in blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator copies Airflow output into an n8n workflow input or file
IF n8n parses that content as instructions or tool parameters
mitigations: Disable manual copy-paste bridges between systems
Add a fixed schema validator before n8n tool execution
Prefix all imported text as untrusted data
Use separate workspaces for Airflow and n8n

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n reads and writes the server filesystem and handles workflow data, while Airflow can make broad network egress calls. If Airflow outputs sensitive data into files or APIs that n8n processes, n8n may expose that data through integrations or logs. The pair has a plausible shared-data path in default deployments, though no PHI is stated.
conditions: IF Airflow writes sensitive workflow artifacts to a location n8n can read
IF an n8n integration node forwards those artifacts to an external service
mitigations: Restrict n8n filesystem access to a dedicated directory
Mask secrets before Airflow emits task outputs
Disable verbose workflow logging in n8n
Review outbound integration nodes for sensitive fields

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is an orchestrator with broad network egress, and n8n can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. Their capabilities overlap on mutable workflow state and external side effects, so concurrent runs can race or overwrite shared artifacts if pointed at the same resources. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or external API resource
IF Airflow-triggered jobs and n8n executions run concurrently without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Add per-run locks or mutex files
Serialize writes to shared downstream systems
Disable shell steps unless required

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate and route task outputs, and n8n’s AI Agent/tooling model can treat workflow inputs as actionable data. If n8n consumes Airflow output without verification, a mistaken or malicious upstream value can cascade into automated API calls or command execution. Because n8n has execute-shell capability, the blast radius can be irreversible and defaults are dangerous.
conditions: IF n8n uses Airflow-produced fields as authoritative tool inputs
IF the workflow includes command, deployment, or external-API actions
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before destructive actions
Validate Airflow outputs against a strict schema
Disable Execute Command nodes for the workflow
Require provenance tags on all upstream fields
Log and diff all tool inputs before execution

E_compliance.rationale: Airflow is source-available and does not declare residency or retention controls here, while n8n stores credentials and workflow data on its server and processes whatever the workflow touches. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for retention, logging, or data residency when regulated data flows through the pair. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from their combined handling of workflow data.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed by an n8n workflow connected to Airflow
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two systems
mitigations: Classify data before routing it into n8n
Set short log retention on n8n
Avoid storing regulated payloads in Airflow task outputs
Document residency and retention for each integration
